evidence: app/app/lib/api.server.ts:49 — cache eviction on rejection must be added before merge

review_cost.rationale: Approvable architecture, but I'd require the cache-eviction fix, the error-boundary rework, and adoption of generated route types — one concrete round of changes.

findings.issue: getJSON caches rejected promises forever (same for the speciesIndex/types/generations/typeMap singletons at lines 82-97, 104-122, 124-136), so a single transient API failure permanently serves that record's error — getRecordOrNull only masks 404, so a 500 becomes a permanent 'Not found' page until process restart.
findings.suggestion: On rejection, delete the entry from the cache (and reset the singleton) so the next request retries; keep the .catch(()=>{}) only to suppress unhandled rejections.

findings.issue: The only ErrorBoundary renders 'Not found' for every error, including API 500s and unexpected exceptions, and hardcodes a Not found title.
findings.suggestion: Use isRouteErrorResponse(err) (or Route.ErrorBoundaryProps) to distinguish 404 from other errors, and render a generic error message for non-404s.

findings.issue: Home-grown 404 pattern: four loaders (move.tsx:11, pokemon.tsx:37, ability.tsx:10, type.tsx:21) return a notFound flag that each component must re-check, instead of the framework's throw data("Not Found", { status: 404 }) + route ErrorBoundary; the not-found UI is rendered from three different places.
findings.suggestion: Throw a 404 data() Response and add a shared per-route ErrorBoundary, deleting components/NotFound.tsx's per-component checks and the duplicated markup in root.tsx.

findings.issue: Route type generation is fully configured (tsconfig rootDirs, typecheck script) but unused: five of seven route components take loaderData: any (pokemon.tsx:182, move.tsx:39, ability.tsx:40, type.tsx:50, types.tsx:12) and loaders hand-type { params, request }.
findings.suggestion: Import Route from './+types/<route>' and use Route.LoaderArgs / Route.ComponentProps so loader return types flow to the components.

findings.issue: The home loader serializes all 1,025 species with their types plus each generation's full species-id list into every document and payload, just to support client-side filtering.
findings.suggestion: Do the filtering in the loader from the URL search params (the framework's recommended shareable-URL pattern), returning only the current page's 48 cards plus counts.

findings.issue: Hidden-ability flags are serialized as an id-keyed object of strings and then reconstructed into a Map in the component (line 43), an awkward boundary detour.
findings.suggestion: Include `hidden: boolean` on each species entry in the loader and read it directly in the card list.

findings.issue: A second import statement from 'react-router' appears below the first one, splitting imports of the same module.
findings.suggestion: Merge into the single existing `import { data } from "react-router"` at line 1.

findings.issue: Rows keyed by `${row.move}-${i}`, using the array index, which can confuse reconciliation when the sort changes row order.
findings.suggestion: Key by a stable composite of move name and level, or precompute a unique id per row in the loader.

findings.issue: Stat bar maxima are hardcoded magic numbers (255 and 1530 at lines 224/234).
findings.suggestion: Name them (MAX_STAT = 255, MAX_TOTAL = 6 * 255) next to STAT_LABELS.

summary: A well-structured, mostly idiomatic React Router 8 framework-mode app with a clean server/client boundary, disciplined small components, and SSR-safe client state. Its main sins are bypassing the framework's typed route modules (five `any`-typed components despite typegen being configured) and its documented throw-404/ErrorBoundary convention, plus one genuine robustness bug: the promise cache never evicts rejections, so a transient API failure permanently poisons data until restart. Mergeable after one focused round of fixes.
